class.name: BulletAttachment2D
class.brief_description: Provides the functionality of bullets being able to carry particles or other nodes as they move.
class.description: Attach this to bullets to carry particles, lights, or any custom nodes along with them. Create a scene rooted at [BulletAttachment2D], pass it to [method BulletVolley2D.bullet_set_attachment] (or the all_bullets_ variant), and override the on_bullet_spawn / on_bullet_enable / on_bullet_disable / on_spawn_in_pool callbacks to set up your nodes for each stage. Attachments are pooled and reused together with their bullets.

method.name: get_applied_time_scale
method.description: The time scale the attachment was last told: the time scale of the volley its bullet belongs to ([member BulletFactory2D.time_scale] times the owner spawner's [member BulletSpawner2D.time_scale] while that lives and has [member BulletSpawner2D.time_scale_affects_volleys] on). 1 means real time and nothing is applied.

method.name: on_bullet_disable
method.description: Executed when the attachment is disabled before it goes to the object pool. You should provide disable logic - attachment gets invisible/disables specific functionality or children etc...

method.name: on_bullet_enable
method.description: Executed when the attachment is enabled again from the object pool. You should provide activation logic - attachment gets visible/enabled etc..

method.name: on_bullet_spawn
method.description:
Executed before the attachment gets added to the scene tree.
Warning: The [BulletAttachment2D] is not yet in the scene tree when this method is executed.

method.name: on_spawn_in_pool
method.description:
Ensure the attachment is in disabled state (example: attachment should be invisible when you are populating the object pool... in the same state as in the [method on_bullet_disable] function).
Warning: The [BulletAttachment2D] is not yet in the scene tree when this method runs, so avoid calls that need configured children. Store that kind of setup in variables and handle it later in [code]_ready[/code].

method.name: on_time_scale_changed
method.description: Executed when the time scale of the bullet changes (also when an attachment is handed to a bullet that runs slowed or sped up, and with 1.0 when it returns to the pool). Use it to slow down anything the plugin cannot scale for you: custom scripts, tweens, shaders. Called whether or not [member apply_time_scale] is on. It is never called while the scale stays 1.

method.name: refresh_time_scale
method.description: Applies the current time scale again to every descendant particle, animated sprite and animation player. Call it after you add such nodes at runtime while the bullet is slowed, otherwise they pick the scale up on the next change.

members.member: When on (default), the plugin multiplies the [code]speed_scale[/code] of every descendant [GPUParticles2D], [CPUParticles2D], [AnimatedSprite2D] and [AnimationPlayer] by the time scale of the bullet, so particles and animations slow down, speed up or pause (scale 0) with it. The authored value is remembered and put back exactly at scale 1; do not change [code]speed_scale[/code] of those nodes from script while a scale is applied (use [method on_time_scale_changed] to follow it yourself). Turn it off to handle everything in [method on_time_scale_changed].
